title: Materials & properties
examples: What is the difference between a natural and a synthetic material?
Can you give an example of a polymer used in construction?
How does the property of flexibility help when choosing a material?

explain.say: Today we will explore different materials and their properties.
Wood is a natural material from trees. It is strong and can be worked by hand.
Metals are often shiny and conduct electricity well. Iron is a common example of a metal.
Polymers are man-made plastics that are very versatile. Polyethylene is a common type of polymer.
Textiles are materials made from fibres, like cotton or wool. They are often woven into fabrics.
Think about building a strong chair. Wood provides structure, and metal might add support joints.

draw.text: Chair: Wood for legs, Metal for joints

faq.q: What is the difference between a polymer and a plastic?
faq.a: A polymer is the general scientific term for a large molecule made of repeating units. Most plastics are polymers, but not all polymers are used as everyday plastics.
asks: What is the relationship between polymers and plastics?

faq.q: Are all metals strong, or can they be weak?
faq.a: Metals can vary greatly in strength depending on the specific metal and how it is treated. Some are very strong, while others are more malleable.

faq.q: What makes a textile different from a polymer?
faq.a: A textile is the finished fabric product, which can be made from many sources, including natural fibres or synthetic polymers. The textile describes the form.
asks: Is a piece of cloth always a polymer?
What is the difference between fibre and textile?

faq.q: Are wood and metal both natural materials?
faq.a: Wood is natural, coming from trees. Metals like iron or copper are mined from the Earth, so they are also considered natural resources, though they must be processed.
asks: Do we have to mine metals?

faq.q: Can you give an example of a polymer that is biodegradable?
faq.a: Some newer polymers are designed to break down safely in the environment. These are sometimes called biodegradable plastics, though this term needs careful definition.
asks: Are all plastics harmful to the environment?

facts: Wood is an organic material, meaning it comes from living things.
Metals are characterized by their high electrical and thermal conductivity.
Polymers are long chains of repeating molecular units.
Textiles are materials made from fibres, which can be natural or synthetic.

quiz.say: Which material is best for making a raincoat that needs to be waterproof and lightweight?
quiz.why: Polymers, like certain plastics, can be manufactured to be highly waterproof and lightweight, making them ideal for rain gear.

wrong.0: Most natural textiles, like cotton, absorb water and lose their insulating properties when wet.
wrong.2: Wood absorbs water and would become heavy and unusable in the rain.
wrong.3: While some metals are waterproof, they are often too heavy or prone to rusting when exposed to moisture.

quiz.say: If you needed a material that is naturally strong and has a visible grain pattern, what would you choose?
quiz.why: Wood comes from trees and has a natural grain pattern, giving it inherent structural strength suitable for furniture.

wrong.1: Metals are strong, but they do not typically display a visible, layered grain pattern like wood.
wrong.2: While polymers can be strong, they are usually manufactured to be uniform and do not possess a natural grain.
wrong.3: Textiles are designed for flexibility and covering, not typically for rigid, structural support showing grain.

quiz.say: A material that is highly flexible, light, and can be woven into a durable fabric would most likely be:
quiz.why: Textiles are defined by being woven fabrics made from fibres, which fits the description of flexibility and being light.

wrong.1: A polymer is the chemical substance; the textile is the finished, woven form of that substance.
wrong.2: Metals are generally rigid and hard, not typically described as flexible and woven.
wrong.3: Wood is a solid structural material, not usually described as being woven into a flexible fabric.
